# Benchmark progress

**Status as of:** Phase 25. Generated from [classical-constants.toml](classical-constants.toml) (50 fixed irrational constants) and [arithmetic-families.toml](arithmetic-families.toml) (27 arithmetic families). See [research-objectives.md](../research-objectives.md) and [SCHEMA.md](SCHEMA.md).

**Evidence legend.** `lean` = Kernel-verified · `lean+paper` = Lean-supported paper proof · `paper` = Paper proof · `external` = External input · `open` = Open.

## Summary by objective (50 fixed constants)

Objective counts overlap (for example, *E*<sub>2</sub> is simply normal, proved nonnormal, and in *K*<sub>2</sub>) and do not sum to 50.

| Objective 3 (Quantify digit distribution) | 14 | `discrepancy_status` other than `open` |
| Objective 3 (Digit-frequency law or bound) | 14 | `digit_frequency_status` other than `open` |
| Objective 4 (Rigorous mathematical limitations) | 17 | `barrier_status = barrier_proved` |
| All five distributional fields open | 35 | `full_normality`, `simple_normality`, `disjunctivity`, `discrepancy_status`, `digit_frequency_status` all `open` |

## Control constants and initially unresolved targets

The roster has two fixed cohorts (see [SCHEMA.md](SCHEMA.md#cohorts)). The 8 **control/reference constants** had their normality or nonnormality in the scope radix settled in the published literature before this research program; they test the methods and do not measure progress on open questions. The 42 **initially unresolved targets** were open in the scope radix when the roster was fixed; counts there measure progress. For a target, a count is credited to a repository registry result when some qualifying property has evidence `lean`, `lean+paper` or `paper` (per-property labels from `radix_results` where recorded), and to external input when every qualifying property rests on a published theorem (`external`). A property without recorded evidence is never counted; the schema check rejects it.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Objective 1 (normality / simple normality) | 3 | 2 | 2 | 0 |
| Objective 2 (nonnormality) | 5 | 5 | 5 | 0 |
| Objective 3 (discrepancy) | 8 | 6 | 6 | 0 |
| Objective 3 (digit-frequency law or bound) | 8 | 6 | 6 | 0 |
| Objective 4 (rigorous limitations) | 0 | 17 | 17 | 0 |

### Pre-program classification of the control constants

The classification that places each control constant in its cohort, from `control_provenance`. It records history, not current evidence: the last column gives the evidence label of the same property in the repository, as shown in the constant and per-radix tables.

| ID | Constant | Basis | Property | Status | Pre-program source | Repository evidence for this property |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BC-33 | Jacobi theta value Θ_3(1/2) | Explicit lacunary 0–1 digits | simple normality | not simply normal | Θ_3(1/2) = 2 + Σ_{n ≥ 2} 2^{−(n² − 1)}: the binary digit 1 occurs exactly at the positions n² − 1, with gaps 2n + 1 → ∞, so the digit 1 has frequency 0 | Lean-supported paper proof |
| BC-34 | Squared theta value Θ_3(1/2)² | Published theorem before the program (External input) | simple normality | not simply normal | Bailey–Borwein–Crandall–Pomerance 2004, Theorem 9.4 and the paragraph after it: the number of ones among the first N binary digits of Θ_3(1/2)² is asymptotic to C_0 N/√(log N) with C_0 ≈ 0.7996, so the digit 1 has frequency 0 | Lean-supported paper proof |
| BC-40 | Multiplicative Lambert series L_{χ_4}(2) | Published theorem before the program (External input) | simple normality | not simply normal | Bailey–Borwein–Crandall–Pomerance 2004, Theorem 9.4 and the paragraph after it: the number of ones among the first N binary digits of Θ_3(1/2)² is asymptotic to C_0 N/√(log N) with C_0 ≈ 0.7996, so the digit 1 has frequency 0; the fractional binary digits of L_{χ_4}(2) = (Θ_3(1/2)² − 1)/4 are those of Θ_3(1/2)² shifted by two places | Lean-supported paper proof |
| BC-45 | Kempner–Fredholm number | Explicit lacunary 0–1 digits | simple normality | not simply normal | Σ_{k ≥ 0} 2^{−2^k}: the binary digit 1 occurs exactly at the positions 2^k, so the digit 1 has frequency 0 | Paper proof |
| BC-46 | Liouville's constant | Explicit lacunary 0–1 digits | simple normality | not simply normal | Σ_{k ≥ 1} 10^{−k!}: only the decimal digits 0 and 1 occur, the digit 1 exactly at the positions k!, so the digit 1 has frequency 0 | Paper proof |
| BC-47 | Champernowne's constant | Published theorem before the program (External input) | normality | normal | Champernowne 1933: normality in base 10 | — (not proved in the repository) |
| BC-48 | Copeland–Erdős constant | Published theorem before the program (External input) | normality | normal | Copeland–Erdős 1946: normality in base 10 of the concatenated primes | — (not proved in the repository) |
| BC-49 | Binary Stoneham constant α(2, 3) | Published theorem before the program (External input) | normality | normal | Stoneham 1973 and Bailey–Crandall 2002: normality of α(2, 3) in base 2 | Kernel-verified |
